status: Property definitions; synthetic Figure 13 values carry no assay units

metrics.name: Equilibrium dissociation constant
metrics.plainEnglish: How tightly does the antibody bind its target?
metrics.interpretation: Lower KD means tighter binding under matched conditions. In a simple 1:1 model, KD = koff / kon.
metrics.measurement: SPR / BLI; model, valency and temperature matter.

metrics.name: Association rate constant
metrics.plainEnglish: How quickly does a binding complex form?
metrics.interpretation: A larger kon means faster association at the same concentration. It is not a direct measure of clinical onset.

metrics.name: Dissociation rate constant
metrics.plainEnglish: How quickly does the antibody let go?
metrics.interpretation: A smaller koff means slower dissociation; ideal 1:1 residence time is 1 / koff. This is not serum half-life or a universal efficacy predictor.

metrics.name: Expression yield
metrics.plainEnglish: Can the cell system make the antibody, and how much?
metrics.interpretation: Yield affects sample supply and production feasibility. Host, format, culture conditions and recovery must be recorded.
metrics.measurement: Expression cultures, titer assays and purification.

metrics.name: Thermal unfolding transition
metrics.plainEnglish: How resistant is the protein to unfolding when heated?
metrics.interpretation: A higher transition temperature suggests greater thermal stability in the tested conditions. It does not directly establish shelf life or in-vivo half-life.
metrics.measurement: nanoDSF / DSF; IgGs can show multiple transitions.

metrics.name: Aggregation
metrics.plainEnglish: Do molecules form larger clusters or particles?
metrics.interpretation: Aggregation can affect formulation and immunogenicity risk. The result depends on concentration, stress and the measurement method.
metrics.measurement: SEC-HPLC, light scattering and particle analysis.

metrics.name: Polyreactivity
metrics.plainEnglish: Does the antibody bind several unrelated non-target materials?
metrics.interpretation: Flags non-specific binding and developability risk. There is no universal score that guarantees clinical failure.
metrics.measurement: Defined non-target binding panels and controls.

metrics.name: Epitope
metrics.plainEnglish: Where on the target does the antibody bind?
metrics.units: Competition bin, residues or structural site
metrics.interpretation: Binding location helps interpret mechanism. A competition bin is not a precise structural epitope or proof of functional effect.
metrics.measurement: SPR / BLI binning, mutagenesis or structural mapping.

metrics.name: Cell potency
metrics.plainEnglish: Does the antibody produce the intended effect in living cells?
metrics.units: EC50 / IC50 plus Emax and assay context
metrics.interpretation: Measures functional activity in the chosen cell model. Target expression, timing and maximum response matter; it does not replace in-vivo or clinical evidence.
metrics.measurement: Reporter assays, flow cytometry and functional cell readouts.
